title: JVM internals and performance — Java Practice
description: Independent practice: Diagnose a service whose memory use grows over time. Seven questions with explanations.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Which tool is appropriate for JVM event recordings?
questions.explanation: Java Flight Recorder captures runtime events for diagnosis.

questions.prompt: Which framework is designed for Java microbenchmarks?
questions.explanation: JMH helps manage JVM-specific benchmarking hazards.
It is a request and does not establish a collection schedule.

questions.prompt: Why can cold single-run timings mislead?

options.text: JIT compilation and warm-up change execution
The wall clock is always constant

questions.explanation: Steady-state behavior may differ from the first invocation.

questions.prompt: What evidence helps diagnose many threads waiting on a lock?

options.text: An image of the source tree
Thread dumps and lock-related runtime events

questions.explanation: Thread state and lock ownership point to contention.

questions.prompt: Is process memory identical to the live Java heap?
questions.explanation: Native allocations, stacks, reserved memory, and other runtime structures also matter.
The map references three arrays. They remain reachable through cache. clear removes those map references. Unreferenced arrays may become eligible for collection; no collection time is promised.
